ko.title: [약리학 #1] 알약을 삼키고 나면 무슨 일이 일어날까? 약리학의 두 갈래

segments.src: > Pharmacology asks two questions: what a drug does to your body (pharmacodynamics), and what your body does to the drug (pharmacokinetics). And every new medicine has to get through a long, costly testing process before it reaches a pharmacy shelf.
segments.tr: > 약리학은 두 가지 질문을 던집니다. 약물이 몸에 무엇을 하는가(약력학, pharmacodynamics), 그리고 몸이 약물에 무엇을 하는가(약동학, pharmacokinetics)입니다. 또한 새로 개발되는 모든 약은 약국 선반에 놓이기 전에 길고 비용이 많이 드는 시험 과정을 거쳐야 합니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: **Pharmacology** is the study of how drugs interact with living things.
segments.tr: **약리학**은 약물이 살아 있는 생명체와 어떻게 상호작용하는지를 연구하는 학문입니다.

segments.src: A "drug" here means any chemical that changes how the body works, whether it's a prescription antibiotic, the caffeine in your coffee, or an over-the-counter pain reliever.
segments.tr: 여기서 '약물'은 몸의 작동 방식을 바꾸는 모든 화학물질을 뜻합니다. 처방 항생제든, 커피 속 카페인이든, 일반의약품 진통제든 모두 포함됩니다.

segments.src: The field splits into two halves.
segments.tr: 이 분야는 두 갈래로 나뉩니다.

segments.src: Each one looks at the same pill from the opposite direction.
segments.tr: 두 갈래는 같은 알약을 서로 반대 방향에서 바라봅니다.

segments.src: Pharmacodynamics: what the drug does to the body**
segments.tr: 약력학: 약물이 몸에 하는 일**

segments.src: Most drugs work by attaching to specific target molecules in the body.
segments.tr: 대부분의 약물은 몸속 특정 표적 분자에 결합해 작용합니다.

segments.src: Many of these targets are **receptors**, which are proteins that normally respond to the body's own chemical signals.
segments.tr: 이 표적 중 많은 것이 **수용체**입니다. 수용체는 몸이 원래 가지고 있는 화학 신호에 반응하는 단백질입니다.

segments.src: Others are enzymes, ion channels, or transporters.
segments.tr: 그 밖의 표적으로는 효소, 이온 통로, 수송체가 있습니다.

segments.src: A drug that switches a receptor on is called an **agonist**.
segments.tr: 수용체를 켜는 약물을 **작용제(agonist)**라고 합니다.

segments.src: A drug that blocks it is called an **antagonist**.
segments.tr: 수용체를 막는 약물은 **길항제(antagonist)**라고 합니다.

segments.src: Pharmacodynamics also asks how strong the effect gets as the dose goes up.
segments.tr: 약력학은 또한 용량을 늘릴 때 효과가 얼마나 강해지는지도 묻습니다.

segments.src: This is the dose-response relationship, and it's the reason "more" isn't always "better."
segments.tr: 이것이 용량-반응 관계이며, 약은 '많을수록 좋다'가 아닌 이유를 설명해 줍니다.

segments.src: Pharmacokinetics: what the body does to the drug**
segments.tr: 약동학: 몸이 약물에 하는 일**

segments.src: From the moment you take a drug, your body starts moving it around and breaking it down.
segments.tr: 약을 복용한 순간부터 몸은 약물을 이동시키고 분해하기 시작합니다.

segments.src: Pharmacologists sum this up as **ADME**:
segments.tr: 약리학자들은 이를 **ADME**로 정리합니다:

segments.src: - **Absorption**: the drug gets into the bloodstream (for a pill, mostly through the gut).
segments.tr: - **흡수(Absorption)**: 약물이 혈류로 들어갑니다(알약이라면 주로 위장관을 통해서입니다).

segments.src: - **Distribution**: the blood carries it to tissues around the body.
segments.tr: - **분포(Distribution)**: 혈액이 약물을 전신의 조직으로 운반합니다.

segments.src: - **Metabolism**: mainly the liver chemically changes it, often into a less active form.
segments.tr: - **대사(Metabolism)**: 주로 간이 약물을 화학적으로 바꾸며, 대개 활성이 약한 형태가 됩니다.

segments.src: - **Excretion**: the body gets rid of it, mostly through the kidneys (urine) or bile.
segments.tr: - **배설(Excretion)**: 몸은 주로 신장(소변)이나 담즙을 통해 약물을 내보냅니다.

segments.src: A key number here is the **half-life**, which is the time it takes for the amount of drug in the blood to fall by half.
segments.tr: 여기서 핵심 수치는 **반감기**입니다. 혈중 약물량이 절반으로 줄어드는 데 걸리는 시간입니다.

segments.src: Half-life helps decide whether a drug is taken once a day or every few hours.
segments.tr: 반감기는 약을 하루 한 번 복용할지, 몇 시간마다 복용할지를 정하는 데 도움을 줍니다.

segments.src: **How a new drug gets made**
segments.tr: **신약이 만들어지는 과정**

segments.src: In the U.S., bringing a new drug to market usually looks like this:
segments.tr: 미국에서 신약을 시장에 내놓는 과정은 보통 다음과 같습니다:

segments.src: 1. **Discovery and preclinical research**: scientists find a promising molecule and test it in the lab and in animals.
segments.tr: 1. **발견 및 전임상 연구**: 과학자들이 유망한 분자를 찾아 실험실과 동물에서 시험합니다.

segments.src: 2. **IND application**: the company asks the FDA for permission to test in humans.
segments.tr: 2. **IND 신청**: 회사가 사람을 대상으로 시험하는 허가를 FDA에 요청합니다.

segments.src: 3. **Phase 1**: a small group, often healthy volunteers, mainly to check safety and dosing.
segments.tr: 3. **1상**: 대개 건강한 자원자 등 소규모 집단을 대상으로 주로 안전성과 용량을 확인합니다.

segments.src: 4. **Phase 2**: a few hundred patients, to see whether the drug works and to keep checking safety.
segments.tr: 4. **2상**: 수백 명의 환자를 대상으로 약이 효과가 있는지 살피고 안전성도 계속 확인합니다.

segments.src: 5. **Phase 3**: hundreds to thousands of patients, often comparing the drug with a placebo or an existing treatment.
segments.tr: 5. **3상**: 수백에서 수천 명의 환자를 대상으로 하며, 종종 위약이나 기존 치료제와 비교합니다.

segments.src: 6. **FDA review**: the company submits the data in a New Drug Application (NDA), and the FDA decides whether to approve it.
segments.tr: 6. **FDA 심사**: 회사가 신약 허가 신청(NDA)으로 자료를 제출하면, FDA가 승인 여부를 결정합니다.

segments.src: 7. **Phase 4 / post-marketing**: safety monitoring continues after the drug is on the market.
segments.tr: 7. **4상 / 시판 후 조사**: 약이 출시된 뒤에도 안전성 감시가 계속됩니다.

segments.src: The whole process often takes 10 to 15 years.
segments.tr: 이 전체 과정은 보통 10~15년이 걸립니다.

segments.src: Most candidates that enter human trials never get approved.
segments.tr: 사람 대상 시험에 들어간 후보 물질 대부분은 결국 승인을 받지 못합니다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: Say you've got a tension headache on a Tuesday afternoon, so you take two regular-strength ibuprofen tablets from the bottle you bought at CVS for about $8.
segments.tr: 화요일 오후에 긴장성 두통이 생겼다고 해 봅시다. 그래서 CVS에서 약 8달러에 산 이부프로펜 병에서 일반 용량 정제 두 알을 꺼내 먹습니다.

segments.src: - **Pharmacodynamics**: ibuprofen blocks enzymes called COX (cyclooxygenase). These enzymes make prostaglandins, chemicals that help produce pain and inflammation. With fewer prostaglandins being made, the headache eases.
segments.tr: - **약력학**: 이부프로펜은 COX(사이클로옥시게나제)라는 효소를 막습니다. 이 효소는 통증과 염증을 일으키는 데 관여하는 화학물질인 프로스타글란딘을 만듭니다. 프로스타글란딘 생성이 줄어들면 두통이 가라앉습니다.

segments.src: - **Pharmacokinetics**: the tablet dissolves and is absorbed through your gut. It typically starts working within about 30 to 60 minutes. Your liver breaks it down, and your kidneys clear what's left. Ibuprofen's half-life is roughly 2 hours, which is part of why the label says you can take another dose every 4 to 6 hours instead of once a day.
segments.tr: - **약동학**: 정제가 녹아 위장관을 통해 흡수됩니다. 보통 약 30~60분 안에 효과가 나타나기 시작합니다. 간이 약물을 분해하고, 신장이 남은 약을 배출합니다. 이부프로펜의 반감기는 약 2시간이며, 이 때문에 라벨에는 하루 한 번이 아니라 4~6시간마다 다시 복용할 수 있다고 적혀 있습니다.

segments.src: That label also comes from the drug development process.
segments.tr: 그 라벨 내용 역시 약 개발 과정에서 나온 것입니다.

segments.src: Its dosing directions and warnings, like the one about stomach bleeding, are based on clinical trials and on years of monitoring after approval.
segments.tr: 복용법과 위장 출혈 같은 경고 문구는 임상시험과 승인 후 수년간의 감시 결과에 근거합니다.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Pharmacodynamics studies what a drug does to the body: which target it binds to and how the effect changes with dose.
segments.tr: 1. 약력학은 약물이 몸에 무엇을 하는지 연구합니다. 어떤 표적에 결합하는지, 그리고 용량에 따라 효과가 어떻게 달라지는지를 다룹니다.

segments.src: 2. Pharmacokinetics studies what the body does to the drug: absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME).
segments.tr: 2. 약동학은 몸이 약물에 무엇을 하는지 연구합니다. 흡수, 분포, 대사, 배설(ADME)입니다.

segments.src: 3. A new drug goes through preclinical research, three phases of human trials, and FDA review. The process often takes more than a decade, and monitoring continues after approval.
segments.tr: 3. 신약은 전임상 연구, 사람 대상 시험 3단계, FDA 심사를 거칩니다. 이 과정은 보통 10년이 넘게 걸리며, 승인 후에도 감시가 계속됩니다.

segments.tr: ## ✅ 자가 점검 퀴즈

segments.tr: (O/X)** 간이 약물을 분해하는 속도는 약력학에서 다루는 질문이다.

segments.src: **Q2.** Which clinical trial phase mainly checks safety in a small group, often healthy volunteers?
segments.tr: **Q2.** 주로 소규모 집단, 흔히 건강한 자원자를 대상으로 안전성을 확인하는 임상시험 단계는 무엇인가?

segments.tr: - A) 1상

segments.tr: - B) 2상

segments.tr: - C) 3상

segments.tr: - D) 4상

segments.tr: **Q3.** 어떤 약물이 수용체에 결합해 몸의 자연 신호가 그것을 켜지 못하도록 막습니다.

segments.tr: 이 약물을 무엇이라고 부르나요?

segments.src: - A) Agonist
segments.tr: - A) 작용제

segments.tr: - B) 길항제

segments.tr: - C) 효소

segments.tr: - D) 대사산물

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Pharmacodynamics**: the study of what a drug does to the body and how it does it.
segments.tr: - **약력학**: 약물이 몸에 무엇을 하며, 그것을 어떻게 하는지 연구하는 학문.

segments.src: - **Pharmacokinetics**: the study of how the body absorbs, distributes, metabolizes, and excretes a drug.
segments.tr: - **약동학**: 몸이 약물을 흡수, 분포, 대사, 배설하는 방식을 연구하는 학문.

segments.src: - **Receptor**: a protein that a drug or natural signal molecule binds to, which triggers or blocks a response.
segments.tr: - **수용체**: 약물이나 몸의 자연 신호 분자가 결합하여 반응을 일으키거나 막는 단백질.

segments.src: - **Half-life**: the time it takes for the amount of drug in the blood to drop by half.
segments.tr: - **반감기**: 혈중 약물량이 절반으로 줄어드는 데 걸리는 시간.

segments.src: - **Clinical trial**: a study in people, run in phases, that tests whether a drug is safe and effective.
segments.tr: - **임상시험**: 사람을 대상으로 여러 단계에 걸쳐 진행하여 약의 안전성과 효과를 검증하는 연구.

segments.src: *Answers: Q1 is X (false).
segments.tr: *정답: Q1은 X(거짓)입니다.

segments.src: Breaking down a drug is metabolism, the "M" in ADME, so it belongs to pharmacokinetics.
segments.tr: 약물을 분해하는 것은 대사이며, 이는 ADME의 'M'이므로 약동학에 속합니다.

segments.src: Q2 is A.
segments.tr: Q2는 A입니다.

segments.src: Phase 1 focuses on safety and dosing in a small group.
segments.tr: 1상은 소규모 집단에서 안전성과 용량에 초점을 맞춥니다.

segments.src: Q3 is B.
segments.tr: Q3은 B입니다.

segments.src: An antagonist occupies the receptor without switching it on, so the body's natural signal can't turn it on either.*
segments.tr: 길항제는 수용체를 켜지 않은 채 점유하므로, 몸의 자연 신호도 수용체를 켜지 못합니다.*

zh.title: [药理学 #1] 吞下那颗药之后会发生什么？药理学的两大分支

segments.src: > Pharmacology asks two questions: what a drug does to your body (pharmacodynamics), and what your body does to the drug (pharmacokinetics). And every new medicine has to get through a long, costly testing process before it reaches a pharmacy shelf.
segments.tr: > 药理学研究两个问题：药物对你的身体做了什么（药效学），以及你的身体对药物做了什么（药代动力学）。而且每一种新药在进入药店货架之前，都必须经过漫长且昂贵的测试流程。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: **Pharmacology** is the study of how drugs interact with living things.
segments.tr: **药理学**是研究药物如何与生物体相互作用的学科。

segments.src: A "drug" here means any chemical that changes how the body works, whether it's a prescription antibiotic, the caffeine in your coffee, or an over-the-counter pain reliever.
segments.tr: 这里的“药物”指任何会改变人体功能的化学物质，无论是处方抗生素、咖啡里的咖啡因，还是非处方止痛药。

segments.src: The field splits into two halves.
segments.tr: 该学科分为两个部分。

segments.src: Each one looks at the same pill from the opposite direction.
segments.tr: 两者从相反的方向审视同一粒药片。

segments.src: Pharmacodynamics: what the drug does to the body**
segments.tr: 药效学：药物对身体做了什么**

segments.src: Most drugs work by attaching to specific target molecules in the body.
segments.tr: 大多数药物通过与体内特定的靶分子结合来发挥作用。

segments.src: Many of these targets are **receptors**, which are proteins that normally respond to the body's own chemical signals.
segments.tr: 其中许多靶点是**受体**，即通常对身体自身化学信号作出反应的蛋白质。

segments.src: Others are enzymes, ion channels, or transporters.
segments.tr: 其他靶点包括酶、离子通道和转运体。

segments.src: A drug that switches a receptor on is called an **agonist**.
segments.tr: 能够激活受体的药物称为**激动剂**。

segments.src: A drug that blocks it is called an **antagonist**.
segments.tr: 能够阻断受体的药物称为**拮抗剂**。

segments.src: Pharmacodynamics also asks how strong the effect gets as the dose goes up.
segments.tr: 药效学还研究剂量增加时效应会如何增强。

segments.src: This is the dose-response relationship, and it's the reason "more" isn't always "better."
segments.tr: 这就是剂量-反应关系，也是“越多越好”并不总是成立的原因。

segments.src: Pharmacokinetics: what the body does to the drug**
segments.tr: 药代动力学：身体对药物做了什么**

segments.src: From the moment you take a drug, your body starts moving it around and breaking it down.
segments.tr: 从你服下药物的那一刻起，身体就开始转运和分解它。

segments.src: Pharmacologists sum this up as **ADME**:
segments.tr: 药理学家用**ADME**概括这一过程：

segments.src: - **Absorption**: the drug gets into the bloodstream (for a pill, mostly through the gut).
segments.tr: - **吸收**：药物进入血液循环（对于口服药片，主要通过肠道）。

segments.src: - **Distribution**: the blood carries it to tissues around the body.
segments.tr: - **分布**：血液将药物输送到全身各组织。

segments.src: - **Metabolism**: mainly the liver chemically changes it, often into a less active form.
segments.tr: - **代谢**：主要由肝脏将药物进行化学转化，通常会变成活性较低的形式。

segments.src: - **Excretion**: the body gets rid of it, mostly through the kidneys (urine) or bile.
segments.tr: - **排泄**：身体将药物排出体外，主要通过肾脏（尿液）或胆汁。

segments.src: A key number here is the **half-life**, which is the time it takes for the amount of drug in the blood to fall by half.
segments.tr: 这里的关键指标是**半衰期**，即血液中药物浓度下降一半所需的时间。

segments.src: Half-life helps decide whether a drug is taken once a day or every few hours.
segments.tr: 半衰期有助于决定一种药物是每天服用一次还是每隔几小时服用一次。

segments.src: **How a new drug gets made**
segments.tr: **新药是如何研发出来的**

segments.src: In the U.S., bringing a new drug to market usually looks like this:
segments.tr: 在美国，一种新药上市通常经过以下流程：

segments.src: 1. **Discovery and preclinical research**: scientists find a promising molecule and test it in the lab and in animals.
segments.tr: 1. **发现与临床前研究**：科学家发现有潜力的分子，并在实验室和动物身上进行测试。

segments.src: 2. **IND application**: the company asks the FDA for permission to test in humans.
segments.tr: 2. **IND申请**：公司向FDA申请获得人体试验许可。

segments.src: 3. **Phase 1**: a small group, often healthy volunteers, mainly to check safety and dosing.
segments.tr: 3. **I期**：小规模试验，通常以健康志愿者为对象，主要用于检验安全性和剂量。

segments.src: 4. **Phase 2**: a few hundred patients, to see whether the drug works and to keep checking safety.
segments.tr: 4. **II期**：数百名患者参与，用于确认药物是否有效，并继续监测安全性。

segments.src: 5. **Phase 3**: hundreds to thousands of patients, often comparing the drug with a placebo or an existing treatment.
segments.tr: 5. **III期**：数百至数千名患者参与，通常将药物与安慰剂或现有治疗方法进行比较。

segments.src: 6. **FDA review**: the company submits the data in a New Drug Application (NDA), and the FDA decides whether to approve it.
segments.tr: 6. **FDA审评**：公司在新药申请（NDA）中提交数据，由FDA决定是否批准。

segments.src: 7. **Phase 4 / post-marketing**: safety monitoring continues after the drug is on the market.
segments.tr: 7. **IV期／上市后研究**：药物上市后仍需持续进行安全性监测。

segments.src: The whole process often takes 10 to 15 years.
segments.tr: 整个过程通常需要10到15年。

segments.src: Most candidates that enter human trials never get approved.
segments.tr: 进入人体试验的候选药物大多数最终都无法获得批准。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活中的例子

segments.src: Say you've got a tension headache on a Tuesday afternoon, so you take two regular-strength ibuprofen tablets from the bottle you bought at CVS for about $8.
segments.tr: 假设你在周二下午因紧张性头痛服用了两片普通强度的布洛芬，这些药是你在CVS药店花约8美元买的。

segments.src: - **Pharmacodynamics**: ibuprofen blocks enzymes called COX (cyclooxygenase). These enzymes make prostaglandins, chemicals that help produce pain and inflammation. With fewer prostaglandins being made, the headache eases.
segments.tr: - **药效学**：布洛芬会抑制一类名为COX（环氧合酶）的酶。这些酶会生成前列腺素，前列腺素是帮助产生疼痛和炎症的化学物质。前列腺素生成减少后，头痛随之缓解。

segments.src: - **Pharmacokinetics**: the tablet dissolves and is absorbed through your gut. It typically starts working within about 30 to 60 minutes. Your liver breaks it down, and your kidneys clear what's left. Ibuprofen's half-life is roughly 2 hours, which is part of why the label says you can take another dose every 4 to 6 hours instead of once a day.
segments.tr: - **药代动力学**：药片溶解后经肠道吸收，通常在约30到60分钟后开始起效。肝脏将其分解，剩余部分由肾脏清除。布洛芬的半衰期约为2小时，这也是为什么说明书写的是每4到6小时可以再服一次，而不是每天一次。

segments.src: That label also comes from the drug development process.
segments.tr: 这份说明书也来自药物研发过程。

segments.src: Its dosing directions and warnings, like the one about stomach bleeding, are based on clinical trials and on years of monitoring after approval.
segments.tr: 其中的用法用量和警告（例如关于胃出血的警告）都是基于临床试验以及批准后多年的监测得出的。

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. Pharmacodynamics studies what a drug does to the body: which target it binds to and how the effect changes with dose.
segments.tr: 1. 药效学研究药物对身体做了什么：它与哪个靶点结合，以及效应如何随剂量变化。

segments.src: 2. Pharmacokinetics studies what the body does to the drug: absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME).
segments.tr: 2. 药代动力学研究身体对药物做了什么：吸收、分布、代谢和排泄（ADME）。

segments.src: 3. A new drug goes through preclinical research, three phases of human trials, and FDA review. The process often takes more than a decade, and monitoring continues after approval.
segments.tr: 3. 新药需要经过临床前研究、三个阶段的人体试验以及FDA审评。整个过程通常超过十年，批准后仍需持续监测。

hi.title: [फार्माकोलॉजी #1] वह गोली निगलने के बाद क्या होता है? फार्माकोलॉजी के दो हिस्से

segments.src: > Pharmacology asks two questions: what a drug does to your body (pharmacodynamics), and what your body does to the drug (pharmacokinetics). And every new medicine has to get through a long, costly testing process before it reaches a pharmacy shelf.
segments.tr: > फार्माकोलॉजी दो सवाल पूछती है: कोई दवा आपके शरीर पर क्या असर करती है (फार्माकोडायनामिक्स), और आपका शरीर दवा के साथ क्या करता है (फार्माकोकाइनेटिक्स)। और हर नई दवा को फार्मेसी की शेल्फ तक पहुँचने से पहले एक लंबी और महंगी परीक्षण प्रक्रिया से गुजरना पड़ता है।

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: **Pharmacology** is the study of how drugs interact with living things.
segments.tr: **फार्माकोलॉजी** वह अध्ययन है कि दवाएँ जीवित प्राणियों के साथ कैसे क्रिया करती हैं।

segments.src: A "drug" here means any chemical that changes how the body works, whether it's a prescription antibiotic, the caffeine in your coffee, or an over-the-counter pain reliever.
segments.tr: यहाँ "दवा" का अर्थ है कोई भी रसायन जो शरीर के काम करने के तरीके को बदलता है, चाहे वह डॉक्टर द्वारा लिखी गई एंटीबायोटिक हो, आपकी कॉफ़ी में मौजूद कैफीन हो, या काउंटर पर मिलने वाली दर्द निवारक दवा हो।

segments.src: The field splits into two halves.
segments.tr: यह क्षेत्र दो हिस्सों में बँटा है।

segments.src: Each one looks at the same pill from the opposite direction.
segments.tr: हर हिस्सा एक ही गोली को विपरीत दिशा से देखता है।

segments.src: Pharmacodynamics: what the drug does to the body**
segments.tr: फार्माकोडायनामिक्स: दवा शरीर पर क्या करती है**

segments.src: Most drugs work by attaching to specific target molecules in the body.
segments.tr: ज़्यादातर दवाएँ शरीर में विशिष्ट लक्ष्य अणुओं से जुड़कर काम करती हैं।

segments.src: Many of these targets are **receptors**, which are proteins that normally respond to the body's own chemical signals.
segments.tr: इनमें से कई लक्ष्य **रिसेप्टर** होते हैं, यानी वे प्रोटीन जो आमतौर पर शरीर के अपने रासायनिक संकेतों पर प्रतिक्रिया देते हैं।

segments.src: Others are enzymes, ion channels, or transporters.
segments.tr: अन्य लक्ष्य एंजाइम, आयन चैनल या ट्रांसपोर्टर होते हैं।

segments.src: A drug that switches a receptor on is called an **agonist**.
segments.tr: जो दवा किसी रिसेप्टर को सक्रिय करती है उसे **एगोनिस्ट** कहते हैं।

segments.src: A drug that blocks it is called an **antagonist**.
segments.tr: जो दवा उसे रोकती है उसे **एंटागोनिस्ट** कहते हैं।

segments.src: Pharmacodynamics also asks how strong the effect gets as the dose goes up.
segments.tr: फार्माकोडायनामिक्स यह भी देखता है कि खुराक बढ़ने पर असर कितना तेज़ होता है।

segments.src: This is the dose-response relationship, and it's the reason "more" isn't always "better."
segments.tr: इसे खुराक-प्रतिक्रिया संबंध कहते हैं, और यही कारण है कि "ज़्यादा" हमेशा "बेहतर" नहीं होता।

segments.src: Pharmacokinetics: what the body does to the drug**
segments.tr: फार्माकोकाइनेटिक्स: शरीर दवा के साथ क्या करता है**

segments.src: From the moment you take a drug, your body starts moving it around and breaking it down.
segments.tr: जैसे ही आप दवा लेते हैं, आपका शरीर उसे इधर-उधर ले जाना और तोड़ना शुरू कर देता है।

segments.src: Pharmacologists sum this up as **ADME**:
segments.tr: फार्माकोलॉजिस्ट इसे **ADME** के रूप में संक्षेप में बताते हैं:

segments.src: - **Absorption**: the drug gets into the bloodstream (for a pill, mostly through the gut).
segments.tr: - **अवशोषण (Absorption)**: दवा रक्तप्रवाह में पहुँचती है (गोली के लिए, मुख्यतः आंत के रास्ते से)।

segments.src: - **Distribution**: the blood carries it to tissues around the body.
segments.tr: - **वितरण (Distribution)**: रक्त उसे शरीर के विभिन्न ऊतकों तक पहुँचाता है।

segments.src: - **Metabolism**: mainly the liver chemically changes it, often into a less active form.
segments.tr: - **चयापचय (Metabolism)**: मुख्यतः यकृत (लिवर) उसे रासायनिक रूप से बदलता है, अक्सर कम सक्रिय रूप में।

segments.src: - **Excretion**: the body gets rid of it, mostly through the kidneys (urine) or bile.
segments.tr: - **उत्सर्जन (Excretion)**: शरीर उसे बाहर निकालता है, मुख्यतः गुर्दों (किडनी, मूत्र) या पित्त के ज़रिए।

segments.src: A key number here is the **half-life**, which is the time it takes for the amount of drug in the blood to fall by half.
segments.tr: यहाँ एक अहम संख्या **अर्ध-आयु (half-life)** है, यानी वह समय जिसमें रक्त में दवा की मात्रा आधी रह जाती है।

segments.src: Half-life helps decide whether a drug is taken once a day or every few hours.
segments.tr: अर्ध-आयु यह तय करने में मदद करती है कि दवा दिन में एक बार लेनी है या हर कुछ घंटों में।

segments.src: **How a new drug gets made**
segments.tr: **नई दवा कैसे बनती है**

segments.src: In the U.S., bringing a new drug to market usually looks like this:
segments.tr: अमेरिका में, किसी नई दवा को बाज़ार में लाने की प्रक्रिया आमतौर पर इस तरह होती है:

segments.src: 1. **Discovery and preclinical research**: scientists find a promising molecule and test it in the lab and in animals.
segments.tr: 1. **खोज और प्रीक्लिनिकल शोध**: वैज्ञानिक एक आशाजनक अणु खोजते हैं और उसे प्रयोगशाला और जानवरों पर परखते हैं।

segments.src: 2. **IND application**: the company asks the FDA for permission to test in humans.
segments.tr: 2. **IND आवेदन**: कंपनी इंसानों पर परीक्षण की अनुमति के लिए FDA से आग्रह करती है।

segments.src: 3. **Phase 1**: a small group, often healthy volunteers, mainly to check safety and dosing.
segments.tr: 3. **फेज़ 1**: एक छोटा समूह, अक्सर स्वस्थ स्वयंसेवक, मुख्यतः सुरक्षा और खुराक जाँचने के लिए।

segments.src: 4. **Phase 2**: a few hundred patients, to see whether the drug works and to keep checking safety.
segments.tr: 4. **फेज़ 2**: कुछ सौ मरीज़, यह देखने के लिए कि दवा काम करती है या नहीं और सुरक्षा की जाँच जारी रहे।

segments.src: 5. **Phase 3**: hundreds to thousands of patients, often comparing the drug with a placebo or an existing treatment.
segments.tr: 5. **फेज़ 3**: सैकड़ों से हज़ारों मरीज़, अक्सर दवा की तुलना प्लेसिबो या मौजूदा इलाज से की जाती है।

segments.src: 6. **FDA review**: the company submits the data in a New Drug Application (NDA), and the FDA decides whether to approve it.
segments.tr: 6. **FDA समीक्षा**: कंपनी न्यू ड्रग एप्लिकेशन (NDA) में डेटा जमा करती है, और FDA तय करती है कि उसे मंज़ूरी दी जाए या नहीं।

segments.src: 7. **Phase 4 / post-marketing**: safety monitoring continues after the drug is on the market.
segments.tr: 7. **फेज़ 4 / बाज़ार-पश्चात**: दवा बाज़ार में आने के बाद भी सुरक्षा की निगरानी जारी रहती है।

segments.src: The whole process often takes 10 to 15 years.
segments.tr: पूरी प्रक्रिया में अक्सर 10 से 15 साल लगते हैं।

segments.src: Most candidates that enter human trials never get approved.
segments.tr: जो अधिकांश उम्मीदवार मानव ट्रायल तक पहुँचते हैं, उन्हें कभी मंज़ूरी नहीं मिलती।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोज़मर्रा की ज़िंदगी में

segments.src: Say you've got a tension headache on a Tuesday afternoon, so you take two regular-strength ibuprofen tablets from the bottle you bought at CVS for about $8.
segments.tr: मान लीजिए मंगलवार दोपहर आपको तनाव वाला सिरदर्द है, तो आप CVS से लगभग $8 में खरीदी बोतल से दो सामान्य-शक्ति वाली इबुप्रोफेन गोलियाँ लेते हैं।

segments.src: - **Pharmacodynamics**: ibuprofen blocks enzymes called COX (cyclooxygenase). These enzymes make prostaglandins, chemicals that help produce pain and inflammation. With fewer prostaglandins being made, the headache eases.
segments.tr: - **फार्माकोडायनामिक्स**: इबुप्रोफेन COX (साइक्लोऑक्सीजिनेज) नाम के एंजाइमों को रोकती है। ये एंजाइम प्रोस्टाग्लैंडिन बनाते हैं, ऐसे रसायन जो दर्द और सूजन पैदा करने में मदद करते हैं। कम प्रोस्टाग्लैंडिन बनने से सिरदर्द कम होता है।

segments.src: - **Pharmacokinetics**: the tablet dissolves and is absorbed through your gut. It typically starts working within about 30 to 60 minutes. Your liver breaks it down, and your kidneys clear what's left. Ibuprofen's half-life is roughly 2 hours, which is part of why the label says you can take another dose every 4 to 6 hours instead of once a day.
segments.tr: - **फार्माकोकाइनेटिक्स**: गोली घुलती है और आंत के ज़रिए अवशोषित होती है। यह आमतौर पर लगभग 30 से 60 मिनट में असर करना शुरू करती है। आपका यकृत इसे तोड़ता है, और बचे हुए अंश को आपकी किडनी बाहर निकालती है। इबुप्रोफेन की अर्ध-आयु लगभग 2 घंटे है, इसी कारण लेबल कहता है कि हर 4 से 6 घंटे में एक और खुराक ली जा सकती है, न कि दिन में एक बार।

segments.src: That label also comes from the drug development process.
segments.tr: वह लेबल दवा विकास की प्रक्रिया से भी आता है।

segments.src: Its dosing directions and warnings, like the one about stomach bleeding, are based on clinical trials and on years of monitoring after approval.
segments.tr: उसके खुराक के निर्देश और चेतावनियाँ, जैसे पेट में रक्तस्राव वाली चेतावनी, क्लिनिकल ट्रायल और मंज़ूरी के बाद वर्षों की निगरानी पर आधारित हैं।

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
1. Pharmacodynamics studies what a drug does to the body: which target it binds to and how the effect changes with dose.
segments.tr: 1. फार्माकोडायनामिक्स बताता है कि दवा शरीर पर क्या करती है: वह किस लक्ष्य से जुड़ती है और खुराक के साथ असर कैसे बदलता है।

segments.src: 2. Pharmacokinetics studies what the body does to the drug: absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME).

es.title: [Farmacología #1] ¿Qué pasa después de tragar esa pastilla? Las dos mitades de la farmacología

segments.src: > Pharmacology asks two questions: what a drug does to your body (pharmacodynamics), and what your body does to the drug (pharmacokinetics). And every new medicine has to get through a long, costly testing process before it reaches a pharmacy shelf.
segments.tr: > La farmacología se plantea dos preguntas: qué le hace un fármaco a tu cuerpo (farmacodinamia) y qué le hace tu cuerpo al fármaco (farmacocinética). Y todo medicamento nuevo debe superar un largo y costoso proceso de pruebas antes de llegar a la estantería de una farmacia.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: **Pharmacology** is the study of how drugs interact with living things.
segments.tr: **La farmacología** es el estudio de cómo interactúan los fármacos con los seres vivos.

segments.src: A "drug" here means any chemical that changes how the body works, whether it's a prescription antibiotic, the caffeine in your coffee, or an over-the-counter pain reliever.
segments.tr: Aquí, un "fármaco" es cualquier sustancia química que modifica el funcionamiento del organismo, ya sea un antibiótico con receta, la cafeína de tu café o un analgésico de venta libre.

segments.src: The field splits into two halves.
segments.tr: El campo se divide en dos mitades.

segments.src: Each one looks at the same pill from the opposite direction.
segments.tr: Cada una observa la misma pastilla desde la dirección opuesta.

segments.src: Pharmacodynamics: what the drug does to the body**
segments.tr: Farmacodinamia: lo que el fármaco le hace al cuerpo**

segments.src: Most drugs work by attaching to specific target molecules in the body.
segments.tr: La mayoría de los fármacos actúan uniéndose a moléculas diana específicas del organismo.

segments.src: Many of these targets are **receptors**, which are proteins that normally respond to the body's own chemical signals.
segments.tr: Muchas de estas dianas son **receptores**, proteínas que normalmente responden a las señales químicas propias del cuerpo.

segments.src: Others are enzymes, ion channels, or transporters.
segments.tr: Otras son enzimas, canales iónicos o transportadores.

segments.src: A drug that switches a receptor on is called an **agonist**.
segments.tr: Un fármaco que activa un receptor se llama **agonista**.

segments.src: A drug that blocks it is called an **antagonist**.
segments.tr: Un fármaco que lo bloquea se llama **antagonista**.

segments.src: Pharmacodynamics also asks how strong the effect gets as the dose goes up.
segments.tr: La farmacodinamia también estudia qué tan intenso se vuelve el efecto a medida que aumenta la dosis.

segments.src: This is the dose-response relationship, and it's the reason "more" isn't always "better."
segments.tr: Esta es la relación dosis-respuesta, y es la razón por la que "más" no siempre significa "mejor".

segments.src: Pharmacokinetics: what the body does to the drug**
segments.tr: Farmacocinética: lo que el cuerpo le hace al fármaco**

segments.src: From the moment you take a drug, your body starts moving it around and breaking it down.
segments.tr: Desde el momento en que tomas un fármaco, tu cuerpo empieza a trasladarlo y a descomponerlo.

segments.src: Pharmacologists sum this up as **ADME**:
segments.tr: Los farmacólogos resumen esto con la sigla **ADME**:

segments.src: - **Absorption**: the drug gets into the bloodstream (for a pill, mostly through the gut).
segments.tr: - **Absorción**: el fármaco pasa al torrente sanguíneo (en el caso de una pastilla, principalmente a través del intestino).

segments.src: - **Distribution**: the blood carries it to tissues around the body.
segments.tr: - **Distribución**: la sangre lo transporta a los tejidos de todo el cuerpo.

segments.src: - **Metabolism**: mainly the liver chemically changes it, often into a less active form.
segments.tr: - **Metabolismo**: principalmente el hígado lo transforma químicamente, a menudo en una forma menos activa.

segments.src: - **Excretion**: the body gets rid of it, mostly through the kidneys (urine) or bile.
segments.tr: - **Excreción**: el cuerpo lo elimina, sobre todo por los riñones (orina) o por la bilis.

segments.src: A key number here is the **half-life**, which is the time it takes for the amount of drug in the blood to fall by half.
segments.tr: Un dato clave aquí es la **vida media**, es decir, el tiempo que tarda la cantidad de fármaco en la sangre en reducirse a la mitad.

segments.src: Half-life helps decide whether a drug is taken once a day or every few hours.
segments.tr: La vida media ayuda a decidir si un fármaco se toma una vez al día o cada pocas horas.

segments.src: **How a new drug gets made**
segments.tr: **Cómo se desarrolla un fármaco nuevo**

segments.src: In the U.S., bringing a new drug to market usually looks like this:
segments.tr: En Estados Unidos, el camino para llevar un fármaco nuevo al mercado suele ser el siguiente:

segments.src: 1. **Discovery and preclinical research**: scientists find a promising molecule and test it in the lab and in animals.
segments.tr: 1. **Descubrimiento e investigación preclínica**: los científicos encuentran una molécula prometedora y la prueban en el laboratorio y en animales.

segments.src: 2. **IND application**: the company asks the FDA for permission to test in humans.
segments.tr: 2. **Solicitud de IND**: la empresa pide permiso a la FDA para hacer pruebas en humanos.

segments.src: 3. **Phase 1**: a small group, often healthy volunteers, mainly to check safety and dosing.
segments.tr: 3. **Fase 1**: un grupo pequeño, a menudo voluntarios sanos, principalmente para verificar la seguridad y la dosis.

segments.src: 4. **Phase 2**: a few hundred patients, to see whether the drug works and to keep checking safety.
segments.tr: 4. **Fase 2**: unos cientos de pacientes, para comprobar si el fármaco funciona y seguir vigilando la seguridad.

segments.src: 5. **Phase 3**: hundreds to thousands of patients, often comparing the drug with a placebo or an existing treatment.
segments.tr: 5. **Fase 3**: cientos o miles de pacientes, a menudo comparando el fármaco con un placebo o con un tratamiento existente.

segments.src: 6. **FDA review**: the company submits the data in a New Drug Application (NDA), and the FDA decides whether to approve it.
segments.tr: 6. **Revisión de la FDA**: la empresa presenta los datos en una Solicitud de Nuevo Fármaco (NDA), y la FDA decide si lo aprueba.

segments.src: 7. **Phase 4 / post-marketing**: safety monitoring continues after the drug is on the market.
segments.tr: 7. **Fase 4 / posterior a la comercialización**: la vigilancia de la seguridad continúa una vez que el fármaco está en el mercado.

segments.src: The whole process often takes 10 to 15 years.
segments.tr: Todo el proceso suele durar entre 10 y 15 años.

segments.src: Most candidates that enter human trials never get approved.
segments.tr: La mayoría de los candidatos que llegan a los ensayos en humanos nunca son aprobados.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: Say you've got a tension headache on a Tuesday afternoon, so you take two regular-strength ibuprofen tablets from the bottle you bought at CVS for about $8.
segments.tr: Imagina que un martes por la tarde tienes un dolor de cabeza tensional, así que tomas dos comprimidos de ibuprofeno de dosis normal del frasco que compraste en CVS por unos 8 dólares.

segments.src: - **Pharmacodynamics**: ibuprofen blocks enzymes called COX (cyclooxygenase). These enzymes make prostaglandins, chemicals that help produce pain and inflammation. With fewer prostaglandins being made, the headache eases.
segments.tr: - **Farmacodinamia**: el ibuprofeno bloquea unas enzimas llamadas COX (ciclooxigenasa). Estas enzimas producen prostaglandinas, sustancias químicas que contribuyen al dolor y a la inflamación. Al producirse menos prostaglandinas, el dolor de cabeza se alivia.

segments.src: - **Pharmacokinetics**: the tablet dissolves and is absorbed through your gut. It typically starts working within about 30 to 60 minutes. Your liver breaks it down, and your kidneys clear what's left. Ibuprofen's half-life is roughly 2 hours, which is part of why the label says you can take another dose every 4 to 6 hours instead of once a day.
segments.tr: - **Farmacocinética**: el comprimido se disuelve y se absorbe a través del intestino. Normalmente empieza a actuar en unos 30 a 60 minutos. El hígado lo descompone y los riñones eliminan lo que queda. La vida media del ibuprofeno es de unas 2 horas, y por eso la etiqueta indica que se puede tomar otra dosis cada 4 a 6 horas en lugar de una vez al día.

segments.src: That label also comes from the drug development process.
segments.tr: Esa etiqueta también es fruto del proceso de desarrollo del fármaco.

segments.src: Its dosing directions and warnings, like the one about stomach bleeding, are based on clinical trials and on years of monitoring after approval.
segments.tr: Sus indicaciones de dosis y advertencias, como la relativa al sangrado estomacal, se basan en ensayos clínicos y en años de vigilancia posterior a la aprobación.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Resumen en 3 líneas

segments.src: 1. Pharmacodynamics studies what a drug does to the body: which target it binds to and how the effect changes with dose.
segments.tr: 1. La farmacodinamia estudia lo que el fármaco le hace al cuerpo: a qué diana se une y cómo cambia el efecto según la dosis.

segments.src: 2. Pharmacokinetics studies what the body does to the drug: absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME).
segments.tr: 2. La farmacocinética estudia lo que el cuerpo le hace al fármaco: absorción, distribución, metabolismo y excreción (ADME).

segments.src: 3. A new drug goes through preclinical research, three phases of human trials, and FDA review. The process often takes more than a decade, and monitoring continues after approval.
segments.tr: 3. Un fármaco nuevo pasa por la investigación preclínica, tres fases de ensayos en humanos y la revisión de la FDA. El proceso suele durar más de una década, y la vigilancia continúa después de la aprobación.

segments.src: - **Absorption**: the drug gets into the bloodstream (for a pill, mostly through the gut).

segments.src: - **Excretion**: the body gets rid of it, mostly through the kidneys (urine) or bile.
segments.tr: - **الإخراج**: يتخلص الجسم من الدواء، وغالبًا عبر الكليتين (البول) أو الصفراء.

segments.src: A key number here is the **half-life**, which is the time it takes for the amount of drug in the blood to fall by half.
segments.tr: ومن الأرقام المهمة هنا **نصف العمر**، أي الزمن اللازم لانخفاض كمية الدواء في الدم إلى النصف.

segments.src: Half-life helps decide whether a drug is taken once a day or every few hours.
segments.tr: ويساعد نصف العمر في تحديد ما إذا كان الدواء يُؤخذ مرة واحدة في اليوم أو كل بضع ساعات.

segments.src: **How a new drug gets made**
segments.tr: **كيف يُطوَّر دواء جديد**

segments.src: In the U.S., bringing a new drug to market usually looks like this:
segments.tr: في الولايات المتحدة، يسير طرح الدواء الجديد إلى السوق عادةً على النحو التالي:

segments.src: 1. **Discovery and preclinical research**: scientists find a promising molecule and test it in the lab and in animals.
segments.tr: 1. **الاكتشاف والبحث ما قبل السريري**: يجد العلماء جزيئًا واعدًا ويختبرونه في المختبر وعلى الحيوانات.

segments.src: 2. **IND application**: the company asks the FDA for permission to test in humans.
segments.tr: 2. **طلب IND**: تطلب الشركة من إدارة الغذاء والدواء الأمريكية (FDA) الإذن بإجراء الاختبار على البشر.

segments.src: 3. **Phase 1**: a small group, often healthy volunteers, mainly to check safety and dosing.
segments.tr: 3. **المرحلة 1**: مجموعة صغيرة، غالبًا من متطوعين أصحاء، والهدف الأساسي التحقق من السلامة وتحديد الجرعة.

segments.src: 4. **Phase 2**: a few hundred patients, to see whether the drug works and to keep checking safety.
segments.tr: 4. **المرحلة 2**: بضع مئات من المرضى، لمعرفة ما إذا كان الدواء فعّالًا مع مواصلة مراقبة السلامة.

segments.src: 5. **Phase 3**: hundreds to thousands of patients, often comparing the drug with a placebo or an existing treatment.
segments.tr: 5. **المرحلة 3**: مئات إلى آلاف المرضى، غالبًا بمقارنة الدواء بدواء وهمي (Placebo) أو بعلاج قائم.

segments.src: 6. **FDA review**: the company submits the data in a New Drug Application (NDA), and the FDA decides whether to approve it.
segments.tr: 6. **مراجعة إدارة الغذاء والدواء**: تقدّم الشركة البيانات في طلب الدواء الجديد (NDA)، فتقرر الإدارة الموافقة عليه أو رفضه.

segments.src: 7. **Phase 4 / post-marketing**: safety monitoring continues after the drug is on the market.
segments.tr: 7. **المرحلة 4 / ما بعد التسويق**: تستمر مراقبة السلامة بعد وصول الدواء إلى السوق.

segments.src: The whole process often takes 10 to 15 years.
segments.tr: وتستغرق العملية كاملةً غالبًا من 10 إلى 15 عامًا.

segments.src: Most candidates that enter human trials never get approved.
segments.tr: ومعظم المرشحين الذين يدخلون التجارب على البشر لا يحصلون على الموافقة أبدًا.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: Say you've got a tension headache on a Tuesday afternoon, so you take two regular-strength ibuprofen tablets from the bottle you bought at CVS for about $8.
segments.tr: لنفترض أنك أصبت بصداع توتري بعد ظهر يوم ثلاثاء، فتناولت قرصين من الإيبوبروفين العادي من العبوة التي اشتريتها من CVS بنحو 8 دولارات.

segments.src: - **Pharmacodynamics**: ibuprofen blocks enzymes called COX (cyclooxygenase). These enzymes make prostaglandins, chemicals that help produce pain and inflammation. With fewer prostaglandins being made, the headache eases.
segments.tr: - **الديناميكا الدوائية**: يحجب الإيبوبروفين إنزيمات تُسمى COX (سيكلوأوكسيجيناز). تصنع هذه الإنزيمات البروستاجلاندينات، وهي مواد كيميائية تساعد على إنتاج الألم والالتهاب. ومع انخفاض إنتاج البروستاجلاندينات، يخف الصداع.

segments.src: - **Pharmacokinetics**: the tablet dissolves and is absorbed through your gut. It typically starts working within about 30 to 60 minutes. Your liver breaks it down, and your kidneys clear what's left. Ibuprofen's half-life is roughly 2 hours, which is part of why the label says you can take another dose every 4 to 6 hours instead of once a day.
segments.tr: - **حركية الدواء**: يذوب القرص ويُمتص عبر الأمعاء، ويبدأ التأثير عادةً خلال نحو 30 إلى 60 دقيقة. يفككه الكبد، وتتخلص الكليتان مما تبقى منه. يبلغ نصف عمر الإيبوبروفين تقريبًا ساعتين، وهذا جزء من سبب ذكر الملصق أنه يمكن تناول جرعة أخرى كل 4 إلى 6 ساعات بدلًا من مرة واحدة في اليوم.

segments.src: That label also comes from the drug development process.
segments.tr: وتأتي تلك التعليمات الموجودة على الملصق أيضًا من عملية تطوير الدواء.

segments.src: Its dosing directions and warnings, like the one about stomach bleeding, are based on clinical trials and on years of monitoring after approval.
segments.tr: فتعليمات الجرعة والتحذيرات فيه، مثل التحذير من النزيف في المعدة، مبنية على التجارب السريرية وعلى سنوات من المراقبة بعد الموافقة.

fr.title: [Pharmacologie n°1] Que se passe-t-il après avoir avalé ce comprimé ? Les deux moitiés de la pharmacologie

segments.src: > Pharmacology asks two questions: what a drug does to your body (pharmacodynamics), and what your body does to the drug (pharmacokinetics). And every new medicine has to get through a long, costly testing process before it reaches a pharmacy shelf.
segments.tr: > La pharmacologie pose deux questions : que fait un médicament à votre organisme (pharmacodynamie), et que fait votre organisme au médicament (pharmacocinétique). Et chaque nouveau médicament doit franchir un long processus d'essais, coûteux, avant d'arriver sur les étagères d'une pharmacie.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concept du jour

segments.src: **Pharmacology** is the study of how drugs interact with living things.
segments.tr: **La pharmacologie** est l'étude de la façon dont les médicaments interagissent avec les êtres vivants.

segments.src: A "drug" here means any chemical that changes how the body works, whether it's a prescription antibiotic, the caffeine in your coffee, or an over-the-counter pain reliever.
segments.tr: Ici, le « médicament » désigne toute substance chimique qui modifie le fonctionnement de l'organisme, qu'il s'agisse d'un antibiotique sur ordonnance, de la caféine de votre café ou d'un antidouleur en vente libre.

segments.src: The field splits into two halves.
segments.tr: Le domaine se divise en deux grandes parties.

segments.src: Each one looks at the same pill from the opposite direction.
segments.tr: Chacune observe le même comprimé sous un angle opposé.

segments.src: Pharmacodynamics: what the drug does to the body**
segments.tr: Pharmacodynamie : ce que le médicament fait à l'organisme**

segments.src: Most drugs work by attaching to specific target molecules in the body.
segments.tr: La plupart des médicaments agissent en se fixant sur des molécules cibles spécifiques de l'organisme.

segments.src: Many of these targets are **receptors**, which are proteins that normally respond to the body's own chemical signals.
segments.tr: Beaucoup de ces cibles sont des **récepteurs**, c'est-à-dire des protéines qui répondent normalement aux signaux chimiques de l'organisme.

segments.src: Others are enzymes, ion channels, or transporters.
segments.tr: D'autres sont des enzymes, des canaux ioniques ou des transporteurs.

segments.src: A drug that switches a receptor on is called an **agonist**.
segments.tr: Un médicament qui active un récepteur est appelé **agoniste**.

segments.src: A drug that blocks it is called an **antagonist**.
segments.tr: Un médicament qui le bloque est appelé **antagoniste**.

segments.src: Pharmacodynamics also asks how strong the effect gets as the dose goes up.
segments.tr: La pharmacodynamie étudie aussi l'intensité de l'effet à mesure que la dose augmente.

segments.src: This is the dose-response relationship, and it's the reason "more" isn't always "better."
segments.tr: C'est la relation dose-effet, et elle explique pourquoi « plus » n'est pas toujours « mieux ».

segments.src: Pharmacokinetics: what the body does to the drug**
segments.tr: Pharmacocinétique : ce que l'organisme fait au médicament**

segments.src: From the moment you take a drug, your body starts moving it around and breaking it down.
segments.tr: Dès que vous prenez un médicament, votre organisme commence à le faire circuler et à le dégrader.

segments.src: Pharmacologists sum this up as **ADME**:
segments.tr: Les pharmacologues résument ce processus par le sigle **ADME** :

segments.src: - **Absorption**: the drug gets into the bloodstream (for a pill, mostly through the gut).
segments.tr: - **Absorption** : le médicament passe dans le sang (pour un comprimé, principalement par l'intestin).

segments.src: - **Distribution**: the blood carries it to tissues around the body.
segments.tr: - **Distribution** : le sang le transporte vers les tissus de tout le corps.

segments.src: - **Metabolism**: mainly the liver chemically changes it, often into a less active form.
segments.tr: - **Métabolisme** : le foie le transforme principalement sur le plan chimique, souvent en une forme moins active.

segments.src: - **Excretion**: the body gets rid of it, mostly through the kidneys (urine) or bile.
segments.tr: - **Élimination** : l'organisme s'en débarrasse, surtout par les reins (urine) ou par la bile.

segments.src: A key number here is the **half-life**, which is the time it takes for the amount of drug in the blood to fall by half.
segments.tr: Un chiffre clé ici est la **demi-vie**, c'est-à-dire le temps nécessaire pour que la quantité de médicament dans le sang diminue de moitié.

segments.src: Half-life helps decide whether a drug is taken once a day or every few hours.
segments.tr: La demi-vie permet de déterminer si un médicament se prend une fois par jour ou toutes les quelques heures.

segments.src: **How a new drug gets made**
segments.tr: **Comment un nouveau médicament est mis au point**

segments.src: In the U.S., bringing a new drug to market usually looks like this:
segments.tr: Aux États-Unis, la mise sur le marché d'un nouveau médicament se déroule généralement ainsi :

segments.src: 1. **Discovery and preclinical research**: scientists find a promising molecule and test it in the lab and in animals.
segments.tr: 1. **Découverte et recherche préclinique** : les scientifiques identifient une molécule prometteuse et la testent en laboratoire et sur l'animal.

segments.src: 2. **IND application**: the company asks the FDA for permission to test in humans.
segments.tr: 2. **Demande d'IND** : l'entreprise demande à la FDA l'autorisation de tester le produit sur l'humain.

segments.src: 3. **Phase 1**: a small group, often healthy volunteers, mainly to check safety and dosing.
segments.tr: 3. **Phase 1** : un petit groupe, souvent de volontaires sains, pour vérifier principalement la sécurité et la posologie.

segments.src: 4. **Phase 2**: a few hundred patients, to see whether the drug works and to keep checking safety.
segments.tr: 4. **Phase 2** : quelques centaines de patients, pour voir si le médicament fonctionne et continuer à surveiller la sécurité.

segments.src: 5. **Phase 3**: hundreds to thousands of patients, often comparing the drug with a placebo or an existing treatment.
segments.tr: 5. **Phase 3** : des centaines à des milliers de patients, souvent comparés à un placebo ou à un traitement existant.

segments.src: 6. **FDA review**: the company submits the data in a New Drug Application (NDA), and the FDA decides whether to approve it.
segments.tr: 6. **Examen par la FDA** : l'entreprise soumet les données dans une demande d'autorisation de mise sur le marché (NDA), et la FDA décide de l'approuver ou non.

segments.src: 7. **Phase 4 / post-marketing**: safety monitoring continues after the drug is on the market.
segments.tr: 7. **Phase 4 / surveillance post-commercialisation** : la surveillance de la sécurité se poursuit une fois le médicament sur le marché.

segments.src: The whole process often takes 10 to 15 years.
segments.tr: L'ensemble du processus dure souvent 10 à 15 ans.

segments.src: Most candidates that enter human trials never get approved.
segments.tr: La plupart des candidats qui entrent dans les essais chez l'humain ne sont jamais approuvés.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dans la vie quotidienne

segments.src: Say you've got a tension headache on a Tuesday afternoon, so you take two regular-strength ibuprofen tablets from the bottle you bought at CVS for about $8.
segments.tr: Imaginons que vous ayez un mal de tête de tension un mardi après-midi, et que vous preniez deux comprimés d'ibuprofène de force standard, tirés du flacon acheté pour environ 8 $ dans une pharmacie CVS.

segments.src: - **Pharmacodynamics**: ibuprofen blocks enzymes called COX (cyclooxygenase). These enzymes make prostaglandins, chemicals that help produce pain and inflammation. With fewer prostaglandins being made, the headache eases.
segments.tr: - **Pharmacodynamie** : l'ibuprofène bloque des enzymes appelées COX (cyclooxygénases). Ces enzymes produisent des prostaglandines, des substances qui contribuent à la douleur et à l'inflammation. Avec moins de prostaglandines produites, le mal de tête s'atténue.

segments.src: - **Pharmacokinetics**: the tablet dissolves and is absorbed through your gut. It typically starts working within about 30 to 60 minutes. Your liver breaks it down, and your kidneys clear what's left. Ibuprofen's half-life is roughly 2 hours, which is part of why the label says you can take another dose every 4 to 6 hours instead of once a day.
segments.tr: - **Pharmacocinétique** : le comprimé se dissout et est absorbé par l'intestin. Il commence généralement à agir au bout de 30 à 60 minutes environ. Le foie le dégrade, et les reins éliminent ce qui reste. La demi-vie de l'ibuprofène est d'environ 2 heures, ce qui explique en partie pourquoi la notice indique qu'on peut reprendre une dose toutes les 4 à 6 heures plutôt qu'une fois par jour.

segments.src: That label also comes from the drug development process.
segments.tr: Cette notice découle également du processus de développement du médicament.

segments.src: Its dosing directions and warnings, like the one about stomach bleeding, are based on clinical trials and on years of monitoring after approval.
segments.tr: Ses posologies et ses mises en garde, comme celle concernant les saignements gastriques, reposent sur les essais cliniques et sur des années de surveillance après l'approbation.

segments.tr: ## Résumé en 3 points

segments.tr: 1. La pharmacodynamie étudie ce que le médicament fait à l'organisme : sur quelle cible il se fixe et comment l'effet varie avec la dose.

segments.src: 2. Pharmacokinetics studies what the body does to the drug: absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME).
segments.tr: 2. La pharmacocinétique étudie ce que l'organisme fait au médicament : absorption, distribution, métabolisme et élimination (ADME).

segments.src: 3. A new drug goes through preclinical research, three phases of human trials, and FDA review. The process often takes more than a decade, and monitoring continues after approval.
segments.tr: 3. Un nouveau médicament passe par la recherche préclinique, trois phases d'essais chez l'humain et l'examen par la FDA. Le processus dure souvent plus de dix ans, et la surveillance se poursuit après l'approbation.

pt.title: [Farmacologia #1] O que acontece depois que você engole esse comprimido? As duas metades da farmacologia

segments.src: > Pharmacology asks two questions: what a drug does to your body (pharmacodynamics), and what your body does to the drug (pharmacokinetics). And every new medicine has to get through a long, costly testing process before it reaches a pharmacy shelf.
segments.tr: > A farmacologia faz duas perguntas: o que um medicamento faz com o seu corpo (farmacodinâmica) e o que o seu corpo faz com o medicamento (farmacocinética). E cada novo medicamento precisa passar por um longo e custoso processo de testes antes de chegar à prateleira da farmácia.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Conceito de hoje

segments.src: **Pharmacology** is the study of how drugs interact with living things.
segments.tr: **Farmacologia** é o estudo de como os fármacos interagem com os seres vivos.

segments.src: A "drug" here means any chemical that changes how the body works, whether it's a prescription antibiotic, the caffeine in your coffee, or an over-the-counter pain reliever.
segments.tr: Aqui, "fármaco" significa qualquer substância química que altera o funcionamento do corpo, seja um antibiótico de receita, a cafeína do seu café ou um analgésico vendido sem prescrição.

segments.src: The field splits into two halves.
segments.tr: O campo se divide em duas metades.

segments.src: Each one looks at the same pill from the opposite direction.
segments.tr: Cada uma observa o mesmo comprimido por uma direção oposta.

segments.src: Pharmacodynamics: what the drug does to the body**
segments.tr: Farmacodinâmica: o que o fármaco faz com o corpo**

segments.src: Most drugs work by attaching to specific target molecules in the body.
segments.tr: A maioria dos fármacos age ligando-se a moléculas-alvo específicas no corpo.

segments.src: Many of these targets are **receptors**, which are proteins that normally respond to the body's own chemical signals.
segments.tr: Muitos desses alvos são **receptores**, proteínas que normalmente respondem aos sinais químicos do próprio corpo.

segments.src: Others are enzymes, ion channels, or transporters.
segments.tr: Outros são enzimas, canais iônicos ou transportadores.

segments.src: A drug that switches a receptor on is called an **agonist**.
segments.tr: Um fármaco que ativa um receptor é chamado de **agonista**.

segments.src: A drug that blocks it is called an **antagonist**.
segments.tr: Um fármaco que o bloqueia é chamado de **antagonista**.

segments.src: Pharmacodynamics also asks how strong the effect gets as the dose goes up.
segments.tr: A farmacodinâmica também investiga quão intenso se torna o efeito conforme a dose aumenta.

segments.src: This is the dose-response relationship, and it's the reason "more" isn't always "better."
segments.tr: Essa é a relação dose-resposta, e é o motivo pelo qual "mais" nem sempre significa "melhor".

segments.src: Pharmacokinetics: what the body does to the drug**
segments.tr: Farmacocinética: o que o corpo faz com o fármaco**

segments.src: From the moment you take a drug, your body starts moving it around and breaking it down.
segments.tr: Desde o momento em que você toma um fármaco, o corpo começa a movimentá-lo e a degradá-lo.

segments.src: Pharmacologists sum this up as **ADME**:
segments.tr: Os farmacologistas resumem isso como **ADME**:

segments.src: - **Absorption**: the drug gets into the bloodstream (for a pill, mostly through the gut).
segments.tr: - **Absorção**: o fármaco passa para a corrente sanguínea (no caso de comprimidos, principalmente pelo intestino).

segments.src: - **Distribution**: the blood carries it to tissues around the body.
segments.tr: - **Distribuição**: o sangue leva o fármaco aos tecidos do corpo.

segments.src: - **Metabolism**: mainly the liver chemically changes it, often into a less active form.
segments.tr: - **Metabolismo**: principalmente o fígado o transforma quimicamente, muitas vezes em uma forma menos ativa.

segments.src: - **Excretion**: the body gets rid of it, mostly through the kidneys (urine) or bile.
segments.tr: - **Excreção**: o corpo elimina o fármaco, principalmente pelos rins (urina) ou pela bile.

segments.src: A key number here is the **half-life**, which is the time it takes for the amount of drug in the blood to fall by half.
segments.tr: Um número-chave aqui é a **meia-vida**, que é o tempo necessário para que a quantidade do fármaco no sangue caia pela metade.

segments.src: Half-life helps decide whether a drug is taken once a day or every few hours.
segments.tr: A meia-vida ajuda a decidir se um fármaco é tomado uma vez por dia ou a cada poucas horas.

segments.src: **How a new drug gets made**
segments.tr: **Como um novo fármaco é desenvolvido**

segments.src: In the U.S., bringing a new drug to market usually looks like this:
segments.tr: Nos EUA, o processo para levar um novo fármaco ao mercado normalmente segue esta sequência:

segments.src: 1. **Discovery and preclinical research**: scientists find a promising molecule and test it in the lab and in animals.
segments.tr: 1. **Descoberta e pesquisa pré-clínica**: cientistas identificam uma molécula promissora e a testam em laboratório e em animais.

segments.src: 2. **IND application**: the company asks the FDA for permission to test in humans.
segments.tr: 2. **Pedido de IND**: a empresa solicita à FDA autorização para testar em humanos.

segments.src: 3. **Phase 1**: a small group, often healthy volunteers, mainly to check safety and dosing.
segments.tr: 3. **Fase 1**: um pequeno grupo, muitas vezes voluntários saudáveis, principalmente para verificar segurança e dosagem.

segments.src: 4. **Phase 2**: a few hundred patients, to see whether the drug works and to keep checking safety.
segments.tr: 4. **Fase 2**: algumas centenas de pacientes, para verificar se o fármaco funciona e continuar monitorando a segurança.

segments.src: 5. **Phase 3**: hundreds to thousands of patients, often comparing the drug with a placebo or an existing treatment.
segments.tr: 5. **Fase 3**: centenas a milhares de pacientes, muitas vezes comparando o fármaco com um placebo ou com um tratamento já existente.

segments.src: 6. **FDA review**: the company submits the data in a New Drug Application (NDA), and the FDA decides whether to approve it.
segments.tr: 6. **Análise da FDA**: a empresa envia os dados em um Pedido de Novo Medicamento (NDA), e a FDA decide se aprova.

segments.src: 7. **Phase 4 / post-marketing**: safety monitoring continues after the drug is on the market.
segments.tr: 7. **Fase 4 / pós-comercialização**: o monitoramento da segurança continua depois que o fármaco chega ao mercado.

segments.src: The whole process often takes 10 to 15 years.
segments.tr: Todo o processo costuma levar de 10 a 15 anos.

segments.src: Most candidates that enter human trials never get approved.
segments.tr: A maioria das candidatas que entram em testes com humanos nunca é aprovada.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## No dia a dia

segments.src: Say you've got a tension headache on a Tuesday afternoon, so you take two regular-strength ibuprofen tablets from the bottle you bought at CVS for about $8.
segments.tr: Suponha que você esteja com uma dor de cabeça tensional numa terça-feira à tarde, então toma dois comprimidos de ibuprofeno de dose regular do frasco que comprou na CVS por cerca de US$ 8.

segments.src: - **Pharmacodynamics**: ibuprofen blocks enzymes called COX (cyclooxygenase). These enzymes make prostaglandins, chemicals that help produce pain and inflammation. With fewer prostaglandins being made, the headache eases.
segments.tr: - **Farmacodinâmica**: o ibuprofeno bloqueia enzimas chamadas COX (ciclo-oxigenase). Essas enzimas produzem prostaglandinas, substâncias que contribuem para a dor e a inflamação. Com menos prostaglandinas sendo produzidas, a dor de cabeça diminui.

segments.src: - **Pharmacokinetics**: the tablet dissolves and is absorbed through your gut. It typically starts working within about 30 to 60 minutes. Your liver breaks it down, and your kidneys clear what's left. Ibuprofen's half-life is roughly 2 hours, which is part of why the label says you can take another dose every 4 to 6 hours instead of once a day.
segments.tr: - **Farmacocinética**: o comprimido se dissolve e é absorvido pelo intestino. Normalmente, ele começa a fazer efeito em cerca de 30 a 60 minutos. O fígado o degrada, e os rins eliminam o que sobra. A meia-vida do ibuprofeno é de aproximadamente 2 horas, o que ajuda a explicar por que a bula diz que você pode tomar outra dose a cada 4 a 6 horas, e não apenas uma vez por dia.

segments.src: That label also comes from the drug development process.
segments.tr: Essa bula também é fruto do processo de desenvolvimento de medicamentos.

segments.src: Its dosing directions and warnings, like the one about stomach bleeding, are based on clinical trials and on years of monitoring after approval.
segments.tr: As instruções de dosagem e os alertas, como o que trata de sangramento no estômago, são baseados em ensaios clínicos e em anos de monitoramento após a aprovação.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Resumo em 3 linhas

segments.src: 1. Pharmacodynamics studies what a drug does to the body: which target it binds to and how the effect changes with dose.
segments.tr: 1. A farmacodinâmica estuda o que o fármaco faz com o corpo: a qual alvo ele se liga e como o efeito muda com a dose.

segments.src: 2. Pharmacokinetics studies what the body does to the drug: absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME).
segments.tr: 2. A farmacocinética estuda o que o corpo faz com o fármaco: absorção, distribuição, metabolismo e excreção (ADME).

segments.src: 3. A new drug goes through preclinical research, three phases of human trials, and FDA review. The process often takes more than a decade, and monitoring continues after approval.
segments.tr: 3. Um novo fármaco passa por pesquisa pré-clínica, três fases de testes em humanos e análise da FDA. O processo costuma levar mais de uma década, e o monitoramento continua após a aprovação.

ja.title: [薬理学 #1] 錠剤を飲んだ後に何が起こるのか？薬理学の二つの柱

segments.src: > Pharmacology asks two questions: what a drug does to your body (pharmacodynamics), and what your body does to the drug (pharmacokinetics). And every new medicine has to get through a long, costly testing process before it reaches a pharmacy shelf.
segments.tr: > 薬理学は二つの問いを投げかけます。薬が体に何をするのか（薬力学、pharmacodynamics）と、体が薬に何をするのか（薬物動態学、pharmacokinetics）です。そして新薬はどれも、薬局の棚に並ぶまでに長く費用のかかる試験過程を通過しなければなりません。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日の概念

segments.src: **Pharmacology** is the study of how drugs interact with living things.
segments.tr: **薬理学**とは、薬物が生体とどのように相互作用するかを研究する学問です。

segments.src: A "drug" here means any chemical that changes how the body works, whether it's a prescription antibiotic, the caffeine in your coffee, or an over-the-counter pain reliever.
segments.tr: ここでいう「薬物」とは、体の働きを変える化学物質すべてを指します。処方抗生物質、コーヒーに含まれるカフェイン、市販の鎮痛薬のいずれも含みます。

segments.src: The field splits into two halves.
segments.tr: この分野は二つに分かれます。

segments.src: Each one looks at the same pill from the opposite direction.
segments.tr: どちらも同じ錠剤を、反対の方向から見ています。

segments.src: Pharmacodynamics: what the drug does to the body**
segments.tr: 薬力学：薬が体に与える作用**

segments.src: Most drugs work by attaching to specific target molecules in the body.
segments.tr: 多くの薬は、体内の特定の標的分子に結合することで作用します。

segments.src: Many of these targets are **receptors**, which are proteins that normally respond to the body's own chemical signals.
segments.tr: これらの標的の多くは**受容体（レセプター）**で、体が本来持つ化学シグナルに反応するタンパク質です。

segments.src: Others are enzymes, ion channels, or transporters.
segments.tr: その他に、酵素、イオンチャネル、輸送体などもあります。

segments.src: A drug that switches a receptor on is called an **agonist**.
segments.tr: 受容体のスイッチを入れる薬は**作動薬（アゴニスト）**と呼ばれます。

segments.src: A drug that blocks it is called an **antagonist**.
segments.tr: 受容体を遮断する薬は**拮抗薬（アンタゴニスト）**と呼ばれます。

segments.src: Pharmacodynamics also asks how strong the effect gets as the dose goes up.
segments.tr: 薬力学はまた、用量を増やすと効果がどこまで強くなるかも問います。

segments.src: This is the dose-response relationship, and it's the reason "more" isn't always "better."
segments.tr: これは用量反応関係であり、「多ければ良い」とは限らない理由です。

segments.src: Pharmacokinetics: what the body does to the drug**
segments.tr: 薬物動態学：体が薬に与える作用**

segments.src: From the moment you take a drug, your body starts moving it around and breaking it down.
segments.tr: 薬を服用した瞬間から、体は薬を移動させ、分解し始めます。

segments.src: Pharmacologists sum this up as **ADME**:
segments.tr: 薬理学者はこれを**ADME**とまとめています。

segments.src: - **Absorption**: the drug gets into the bloodstream (for a pill, mostly through the gut).
segments.tr: - **吸収（Absorption）**：薬が血液中に入ること（錠剤の場合は主に腸管を通じて）。

segments.src: - **Distribution**: the blood carries it to tissues around the body.
segments.tr: - **分布（Distribution）**：血液が薬を全身の組織へ運ぶこと。

segments.src: - **Metabolism**: mainly the liver chemically changes it, often into a less active form.
segments.tr: - **代謝（Metabolism）**：主に肝臓が化学的に変化させ、多くは活性の低い形になること。

segments.src: - **Excretion**: the body gets rid of it, mostly through the kidneys (urine) or bile.
segments.tr: - **排泄（Excretion）**：体が薬を外へ出すこと。主に腎臓（尿）または胆汁を通じて。

segments.src: A key number here is the **half-life**, which is the time it takes for the amount of drug in the blood to fall by half.
segments.tr: ここで重要な数値が**半減期**です。血中の薬物量が半分に減るまでの時間を指します。

segments.src: Half-life helps decide whether a drug is taken once a day or every few hours.
segments.tr: 半減期によって、薬を1日1回にするか、数時間ごとに飲むかが決まります。

segments.src: **How a new drug gets made**
segments.tr: **新薬が作られる過程**

segments.src: In the U.S., bringing a new drug to market usually looks like this:
segments.tr: 米国では、新薬を市場に出すまでの流れは通常次のとおりです。

segments.src: 1. **Discovery and preclinical research**: scientists find a promising molecule and test it in the lab and in animals.
segments.tr: 1. **発見と前臨床研究**：科学者が有望な分子を見つけ、実験室や動物で試験します。

segments.src: 2. **IND application**: the company asks the FDA for permission to test in humans.
segments.tr: 2. **IND申請**：企業がFDAに対し、ヒトでの試験の許可を求めます。

segments.src: 3. **Phase 1**: a small group, often healthy volunteers, mainly to check safety and dosing.
segments.tr: 3. **第1相**：少数の被験者（多くは健康なボランティア）で、主に安全性と用量を確認します。

segments.src: 4. **Phase 2**: a few hundred patients, to see whether the drug works and to keep checking safety.
segments.tr: 4. **第2相**：数百人の患者で、薬が効くかどうかを確認し、安全性の監視を続けます。

segments.src: 5. **Phase 3**: hundreds to thousands of patients, often comparing the drug with a placebo or an existing treatment.
segments.tr: 5. **第3相**：数百人から数千人の患者で、プラセボや既存治療と比較することが多いです。

segments.src: 6. **FDA review**: the company submits the data in a New Drug Application (NDA), and the FDA decides whether to approve it.
segments.tr: 6. **FDA審査**：企業は新薬承認申請（NDA）でデータを提出し、FDAが承認するかどうかを判断します。

segments.src: 7. **Phase 4 / post-marketing**: safety monitoring continues after the drug is on the market.
segments.tr: 7. **第4相／市販後調査**：薬が市場に出た後も安全性の監視が続けられます。

segments.src: The whole process often takes 10 to 15 years.
segments.tr: この全過程には、10年から15年かかることが多いです。

segments.src: Most candidates that enter human trials never get approved.
segments.tr: ヒト試験に進んだ候補薬の大半は、最終的に承認されません。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活での例

segments.src: Say you've got a tension headache on a Tuesday afternoon, so you take two regular-strength ibuprofen tablets from the bottle you bought at CVS for about $8.
segments.tr: 火曜日の午後に緊張型頭痛がしたとします。CVSで約8ドルで買った瓶から、通常量のイブプロフェン錠を2錠飲みます。

segments.src: - **Pharmacodynamics**: ibuprofen blocks enzymes called COX (cyclooxygenase). These enzymes make prostaglandins, chemicals that help produce pain and inflammation. With fewer prostaglandins being made, the headache eases.
segments.tr: - **薬力学**：イブプロフェンは、COX（シクロオキシゲナーゼ）と呼ばれる酵素を阻害します。この酵素はプロスタグランジンを作ります。プロスタグランジンは痛みや炎症を生じさせる化学物質です。産生が減ると、頭痛が和らぎます。

segments.src: - **Pharmacokinetics**: the tablet dissolves and is absorbed through your gut. It typically starts working within about 30 to 60 minutes. Your liver breaks it down, and your kidneys clear what's left. Ibuprofen's half-life is roughly 2 hours, which is part of why the label says you can take another dose every 4 to 6 hours instead of once a day.
segments.tr: - **薬物動態学**：錠剤は溶解して腸から吸収されます。通常、効き始めるまでおよそ30〜60分かかります。肝臓が薬を分解し、残ったものは腎臓が排泄します。イブプロフェンの半減期はおよそ2時間で、添付文書で1日1回ではなく4〜6時間ごとの服用が認められている理由の一つです。

segments.src: That label also comes from the drug development process.
segments.tr: その添付文書の内容も、薬の開発過程から来ています。

segments.src: Its dosing directions and warnings, like the one about stomach bleeding, are based on clinical trials and on years of monitoring after approval.
segments.tr: 用法・用量や胃出血などの警告は、臨床試験と承認後の長年の監視に基づいています。

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3行まとめ

segments.src: 1. Pharmacodynamics studies what a drug does to the body: which target it binds to and how the effect changes with dose.
segments.tr: 1. 薬力学は、薬が体に何をするかを研究します。どの標的に結合し、用量によって効果がどう変わるかです。

segments.src: 2. Pharmacokinetics studies what the body does to the drug: absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME).
segments.tr: 2. 薬物動態学は、体が薬に何をするかを研究します。吸収、分布、代謝、排泄（ADME）です。

segments.src: 3. A new drug goes through preclinical research, three phases of human trials, and FDA review. The process often takes more than a decade, and monitoring continues after approval.
segments.tr: 3. 新薬は、前臨床研究、3段階のヒト試験、FDA審査を経ます。この過程は10年以上かかることが多く、承認後も監視が続けられます。

segments.src: - **Pharmacokinetics**: the tablet dissolves and is absorbed through your gut. It typically starts working within about 30 to 60 minutes. Your liver breaks it down, and your kidneys clear what's left. Ibuprofen's half-life is roughly 2 hours, which is part of why the label says you can take another dose every 4 to 6 hours instead of once a day.
segments.tr: - **Pharmakokinetik**: Die Tablette löst sich auf und wird über den Darm resorbiert. Sie beginnt in der Regel innerhalb von etwa 30 bis 60 Minuten zu wirken. Die Leber baut sie ab, und die Nieren scheiden den Rest aus. Die Halbwertszeit von Ibuprofen beträgt etwa 2 Stunden, weshalb auf der Packung steht, dass man alle 4 bis 6 Stunden erneut dosieren darf und nicht nur einmal am Tag.

segments.src: That label also comes from the drug development process.
segments.tr: Diese Packungsangabe stammt ebenfalls aus dem Entwicklungsprozess des Arzneimittels.

segments.src: Its dosing directions and warnings, like the one about stomach bleeding, are based on clinical trials and on years of monitoring after approval.
segments.tr: Die Dosierungshinweise und Warnungen, etwa die zu Magenblutungen, beruhen auf klinischen Studien und auf jahrelanger Überwachung nach der Zulassung.

vi.title: [Dược lý #1] Sau khi nuốt viên thuốc đó thì điều gì xảy ra? Hai nửa của dược lý học

segments.src: > Pharmacology asks two questions: what a drug does to your body (pharmacodynamics), and what your body does to the drug (pharmacokinetics). And every new medicine has to get through a long, costly testing process before it reaches a pharmacy shelf.
segments.tr: > Dược lý học đặt ra hai câu hỏi: thuốc tác động gì lên cơ thể bạn (dược lực học), và cơ thể bạn tác động gì lên thuốc (dược động học). Và mọi loại thuốc mới đều phải trải qua một quy trình thử nghiệm dài và tốn kém trước khi có mặt trên kệ nhà thuốc.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Khái niệm hôm nay

segments.src: **Pharmacology** is the study of how drugs interact with living things.
segments.tr: **Dược lý học** là ngành nghiên cứu cách thuốc tương tác với các sinh vật sống.

segments.src: A "drug" here means any chemical that changes how the body works, whether it's a prescription antibiotic, the caffeine in your coffee, or an over-the-counter pain reliever.
segments.tr: “Thuốc” ở đây là bất kỳ hóa chất nào làm thay đổi hoạt động của cơ thể, dù là kháng sinh kê đơn, caffeine trong cà phê của bạn, hay thuốc giảm đau không kê đơn.

segments.src: The field splits into two halves.
segments.tr: Ngành này được chia thành hai nửa.

segments.src: Each one looks at the same pill from the opposite direction.
segments.tr: Mỗi nửa nhìn cùng một viên thuốc từ hai hướng ngược nhau.

segments.src: Pharmacodynamics: what the drug does to the body**
segments.tr: Dược lực học: thuốc tác động gì lên cơ thể**

segments.src: Most drugs work by attaching to specific target molecules in the body.
segments.tr: Phần lớn thuốc hoạt động bằng cách gắn vào các phân tử đích đặc hiệu trong cơ thể.

segments.src: Many of these targets are **receptors**, which are proteins that normally respond to the body's own chemical signals.
segments.tr: Nhiều đích trong số này là **thụ thể (receptor)**, tức là các protein thường đáp ứng với tín hiệu hóa học của chính cơ thể.

segments.src: Others are enzymes, ion channels, or transporters.
segments.tr: Những đích khác là enzyme, kênh ion hoặc chất vận chuyển.

segments.src: A drug that switches a receptor on is called an **agonist**.
segments.tr: Thuốc kích hoạt thụ thể được gọi là **chất chủ vận (agonist)**.

segments.src: A drug that blocks it is called an **antagonist**.
segments.tr: Thuốc chặn thụ thể được gọi là **chất đối kháng (antagonist)**.

segments.src: Pharmacodynamics also asks how strong the effect gets as the dose goes up.
segments.tr: Dược lực học cũng xem xét hiệu quả tăng mạnh đến mức nào khi liều tăng.

segments.src: This is the dose-response relationship, and it's the reason "more" isn't always "better."
segments.tr: Đây là mối quan hệ liều-đáp ứng, và cũng là lý do vì sao “nhiều hơn” không phải lúc nào cũng “tốt hơn”.

segments.src: Pharmacokinetics: what the body does to the drug**
segments.tr: Dược động học: cơ thể tác động gì lên thuốc**

segments.src: From the moment you take a drug, your body starts moving it around and breaking it down.
segments.tr: Từ thời điểm bạn uống thuốc, cơ thể bắt đầu di chuyển và phân hủy thuốc.

segments.src: Pharmacologists sum this up as **ADME**:
segments.tr: Các nhà dược lý học tóm tắt quá trình này bằng **ADME**:

segments.src: - **Absorption**: the drug gets into the bloodstream (for a pill, mostly through the gut).
segments.tr: - **Hấp thu (Absorption)**: thuốc đi vào máu (với viên uống, chủ yếu qua đường ruột).

segments.src: - **Distribution**: the blood carries it to tissues around the body.
segments.tr: - **Phân bố (Distribution)**: máu mang thuốc đến các mô trên khắp cơ thể.

segments.src: - **Metabolism**: mainly the liver chemically changes it, often into a less active form.
segments.tr: - **Chuyển hóa (Metabolism)**: chủ yếu là gan biến đổi thuốc về mặt hóa học, thường thành dạng ít hoạt tính hơn.

segments.src: - **Excretion**: the body gets rid of it, mostly through the kidneys (urine) or bile.
segments.tr: - **Thải trừ (Excretion)**: cơ thể loại bỏ thuốc, chủ yếu qua thận (nước tiểu) hoặc mật.

segments.src: A key number here is the **half-life**, which is the time it takes for the amount of drug in the blood to fall by half.
segments.tr: Một con số quan trọng ở đây là **thời gian bán thải (half-life)**, tức là thời gian để lượng thuốc trong máu giảm còn một nửa.

segments.src: Half-life helps decide whether a drug is taken once a day or every few hours.
segments.tr: Thời gian bán thải giúp quyết định thuốc được uống một lần mỗi ngày hay cách vài giờ một lần.

segments.src: **How a new drug gets made**
segments.tr: **Một loại thuốc mới được tạo ra như thế nào**

segments.src: In the U.S., bringing a new drug to market usually looks like this:
segments.tr: Ở Hoa Kỳ, quá trình đưa một loại thuốc mới ra thị trường thường diễn ra như sau:

segments.src: 1. **Discovery and preclinical research**: scientists find a promising molecule and test it in the lab and in animals.
segments.tr: 1. **Phát hiện và nghiên cứu tiền lâm sàng**: các nhà khoa học tìm ra một phân tử có triển vọng và thử nghiệm trong phòng thí nghiệm cũng như trên động vật.

segments.src: 2. **IND application**: the company asks the FDA for permission to test in humans.
segments.tr: 2. **Hồ sơ IND**: công ty xin phép FDA để thử nghiệm trên người.

segments.src: 3. **Phase 1**: a small group, often healthy volunteers, mainly to check safety and dosing.
segments.tr: 3. **Giai đoạn 1**: nhóm nhỏ, thường là người tình nguyện khỏe mạnh, chủ yếu để kiểm tra độ an toàn và liều dùng.

segments.src: 4. **Phase 2**: a few hundred patients, to see whether the drug works and to keep checking safety.
segments.tr: 4. **Giai đoạn 2**: vài trăm bệnh nhân, để xem thuốc có hiệu quả không và tiếp tục theo dõi độ an toàn.

segments.src: 5. **Phase 3**: hundreds to thousands of patients, often comparing the drug with a placebo or an existing treatment.
segments.tr: 5. **Giai đoạn 3**: hàng trăm đến hàng nghìn bệnh nhân, thường so sánh thuốc với giả dược hoặc phương pháp điều trị hiện có.

segments.src: 6. **FDA review**: the company submits the data in a New Drug Application (NDA), and the FDA decides whether to approve it.
segments.tr: 6. **FDA xem xét**: công ty nộp dữ liệu trong Hồ sơ đăng ký thuốc mới (NDA), và FDA quyết định có phê duyệt hay không.

segments.src: 7. **Phase 4 / post-marketing**: safety monitoring continues after the drug is on the market.
segments.tr: 7. **Giai đoạn 4 / sau khi lưu hành**: tiếp tục giám sát an toàn sau khi thuốc đã có mặt trên thị trường.

segments.src: The whole process often takes 10 to 15 years.
segments.tr: Toàn bộ quá trình thường mất 10 đến 15 năm.

segments.src: Most candidates that enter human trials never get approved.
segments.tr: Phần lớn các ứng viên bước vào thử nghiệm trên người không bao giờ được phê duyệt.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Trong đời sống hằng ngày

segments.src: Say you've got a tension headache on a Tuesday afternoon, so you take two regular-strength ibuprofen tablets from the bottle you bought at CVS for about $8.
segments.tr: Giả sử vào một buổi chiều thứ Ba, bạn bị đau đầu căng thẳng, nên bạn uống hai viên ibuprofen liều thông thường lấy từ hộp mua ở CVS với giá khoảng 8 đô la.

segments.src: - **Pharmacodynamics**: ibuprofen blocks enzymes called COX (cyclooxygenase). These enzymes make prostaglandins, chemicals that help produce pain and inflammation. With fewer prostaglandins being made, the headache eases.
segments.tr: - **Dược lực học**: ibuprofen ức chế các enzyme gọi là COX (cyclooxygenase). Các enzyme này tạo ra prostaglandin, những chất góp phần gây đau và viêm. Khi sinh ra ít prostaglandin hơn, cơn đau đầu dịu đi.

segments.src: - **Pharmacokinetics**: the tablet dissolves and is absorbed through your gut. It typically starts working within about 30 to 60 minutes. Your liver breaks it down, and your kidneys clear what's left. Ibuprofen's half-life is roughly 2 hours, which is part of why the label says you can take another dose every 4 to 6 hours instead of once a day.
segments.tr: - **Dược động học**: viên thuốc tan ra và được hấp thu qua ruột. Thuốc thường bắt đầu có tác dụng sau khoảng 30 đến 60 phút. Gan phân hủy thuốc, và thận đào thải phần còn lại. Thời gian bán thải của ibuprofen khoảng 2 giờ, đó là một phần lý do nhãn thuốc ghi rằng có thể uống liều tiếp theo sau mỗi 4 đến 6 giờ thay vì một lần mỗi ngày.

segments.src: That label also comes from the drug development process.
segments.tr: Nhãn thuốc đó cũng bắt nguồn từ quá trình phát triển thuốc.

segments.src: Its dosing directions and warnings, like the one about stomach bleeding, are based on clinical trials and on years of monitoring after approval.
segments.tr: Hướng dẫn liều dùng và cảnh báo, như cảnh báo về chảy máu dạ dày, đều dựa trên các thử nghiệm lâm sàng và nhiều năm giám sát sau khi thuốc được phê duyệt.

segments.tr: 1. Dược lực học nghiên cứu thuốc tác động gì lên cơ thể: thuốc gắn vào đích nào và hiệu quả thay đổi thế nào theo liều.
